justification: The accountability adapter validates managed Markdown markers and GitHub issue labels; these protocol strings are not domain representations.

Test-only: the repeated rows are `git` argument vectors and arms of a shell `gh` stub that model GitHub protocol responses. They are fixture data for one forged-comment scenario, not production dispatch logic.

Each branch validates a different typed model (initiative, definition, workspace, plan, graph) whose validate() has its own signature and error shape; there is no common row type to tabulate, and the graph arm maps violations rather than extending directly.
Hand-rolled parser for the flat portfolio-manifest subset; each field is its own literal prefix (id:/capability:/path:) rather than a shared shape that a table could carry.

Test-only fixture builder: the repeated rows are fake GitHub CLI responses keyed by command, the same shape already allowlisted for autonomous_integration_base_sync.rs. Attribution moved to this function when #3472 fixed function_ranges_brace().
This integration test reads Rust source and asserts command output; std::time plus substring assertions trigger the file-scoped heuristic without encoding domain logic.
This test-only fixture dispatches exact fake GitHub CLI responses; the repeated shell case arms model protocol commands rather than production domain logic.
This integration test asserts diagnostic text; its substring checks do not encode runtime domain meaning.
This helper parses a labeled CLI help section; its string operations inspect presentation structure rather than encode domain logic.
This test-only command factory and its assertion fixtures contain command-output strings, not domain representation logic.
The test helper asserts command output, not a domain representation; this inherited file-scoped heuristic result remains intentionally allowlisted.

The arms match distinct EditAction variants with different bindings and different guard policies; the inner ifs each raise a differently named violation with its own message. A table would have to carry a closure per row and would hide which policy produced which violation id.

Shell-source scanner branching on distinct bash syntax prefixes (function / source / export) to bucket symbols, dependencies, and interfaces; the branches have different payloads, not one repeated shape.

The genuinely uniform part — the four signal penalties — is already a table with a single dispatcher loop. The remaining branches each apply a different scoring formula (flat credit, clamped coverage ratio, cache-hit rate, churn ratio) to a different field, so they share no row shape.

The branches are cumulative escalation thresholds, not parallel cases: each adds a different role set to the same accumulator, one arm removes a role, and one returns early. Order is semantic, so a predicate table would change behaviour.
Test assertions pinning the exact status-line wording (skip reasons, deficiency labels); the strings are the protocol under test, not domain encoding.
Test assertions pinning the exact verdict-line wording (pass-load phrases); the strings are the protocol under test, not domain encoding.
Positional RFC3339 byte parser; the repeated branches check fixed-offset separator bytes ('-', 'T', ':') and are the format grammar, not copy-pasted logic.
Top-level contract validate() delegating to one validate() per optional nested field; each call names a distinct field, not a repeated structural branch.
Metadata-block parser; each branch matches a distinct literal field prefix (issue:, ...) with its own payload handling, not one repeated shape.
Test assertions pinning the exact repair-report line wording (missing counts, ALERT marker); the strings are the protocol under test, not domain encoding.
Test assertions on the wording of proposed-action safety reasons (invariant labels); the strings are the protocol under test, not domain encoding.
Well-known-filename classifier; each branch names a distinct file name (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, ...) mapped to a distinct FileType, i.e. a name table in branch form.
The structural validator scans static skill text for required contract vocabulary; it does not encode runtime domain meaning from free-form names.
Test fixtures and assertions for signature normalization (path/number masking); the literals are test inputs and expected output, not domain logic.
Test fixtures and assertions for event-log normalization (ISO-8601 error wording); the literals are test inputs and expected output, not domain logic.
